entities.summary: Tuvan throat singing, also known as Mongolian throat singing, is a style of singing, the main technique of which is known as khoomei. It is practiced by people in Tuva, Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, Xinjiang Mongol regions such as Bortala Mongol Autonomous Prefecture and Bayingolin Mongol Autonomous Prefecture, Buryatia, Kalmykia and Altay. It is noted for including overtone singing. In 2009, Tuvan throat singing was included in the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity of UNESCO.
